gameVerifiedNote: Static evidence only, and the a-hud row is the one row in this slice whose correctness is mostly a rendering question. Every member named below is read from the interop build of the Forge-MapEditor-QA profile and every use of it is compiled against those same assemblies (see `compileCheck`), both placements are the game's own readouts rather than ones this provider draws, and every point that only a running game can settle is listed as unverified rather than assumed.
question: Can one author node show a number on the game's own readouts at the two places the checklist names, in the four forms it names, in a colour, to an audience that can be the whole team or one player?

answers.status_bar: Yes, through the game's own local status readout. `GuiManager.Current.m_playerLayer.m_playerStatus` is the local player's own status area; `UpdateShield(float)` writes its shield bar, `m_shieldText` is the number field that sits beside it, and `m_shieldUIParent` is the group switch that shows or hides the pair. The checklist's own example ('护盾 45 / 100' beside the health bar) is this readout, which is why it is the implemented placement rather than a new UI stack.
answers.teammate_overhead: Yes, by the shape the repository already ships. A `NavMarker` carries four text meshes (`m_title`, `m_playerName`, `m_distance`, `m_signInfo`) and no more, so a second line is a clone of `NavMarker.m_playerName` parented to the name mesh, positioned from the name's own local `textBounds`. The line is re-applied from `PlaceNavMarkerOnGO.UpdateExtraInfo`, which is the member the game itself refreshes a player's marker from, and `PlaceNavMarkerOnGO.m_extraInfoVisible` — the flag the native extra-information row shares with the game's rescue and resource hints — is saved the first time a line takes it over and put back when the line goes away, when the world is replaced and when the marker is destroyed. That is `InfiniTweaks.ResourceHud`/`ResourceHudView`'s own design, and it is why this placement is implemented rather than refused.
answers.audience: Both. `team` draws on every addressed client. `self` means the value belongs to one player, and that player's own session travels with the command: the handler draws only when that session is `SNet.LocalPlayer.Lookup` — the same value the network layer compares an inbound presentation request's endpoint against (`NetworkCommandRouting.IsPresentationRequest`) — and answers `hud-audience-not-addressed` on any other machine. The one combination that is refused by name is `self` with `placement=teammate_overhead`: the local player has no overhead marker, so the two members cannot both be true of one row.
answers.speaker: `a-p-say` names its speaker as a player entity rather than a slot index. The conversion is `PlayerSessions.SlotOf`, which reads the agent the entity resolves to through `PlayerIdentityModule.CurrentAgent` and asks that agent's own `Owner.PlayerSlotIndex()`; `PlayerVoiceManager.WantToSay(slot, eventId)` still takes the number, because that is what the game's entry takes.
answers.form: All four, with one placement limit: `number`, `number_of_max` and `percent` render text, and `bar` writes the game's own bar without text. Only the status bar has a bar sprite, so `bar` on the teammate overhead is refused by name.
answers.colour: `#rrggbb`, written to the text component's own colour. Absent means the game's own colour is left alone. The marker clone deliberately does not depend on TMP rich text: it disables `overrideColorTags` and vertex gradients precisely because a cloned TMP would otherwise inherit the source's own colours.

wiring.hooks: ForgeMap/Native/TeammateOverheadHooks.cs declares three patches the integration batch adds to `MapNativeHooks.Types`: a `[HarmonyPostfix, HarmonyPriority(Priority.Last)]` on `PlaceNavMarkerOnGO.UpdateExtraInfo` (re-apply the stored line), one on `PlaceNavMarkerOnGO.OnDestroy` (forget the marker), and a `[HarmonyPrefix]` on `PlaceNavMarkerOnGO.SetExtraInfoVisible` (defer the native change while a line is showing).
wiring.sessionConversion: ForgeMap/Native/PlayerSessions.cs answers player-entity -> session (`SNet_Player.Lookup`), player-entity -> slot and player-entity -> is-local. It needs one method on the shared `PlayerIdentityModule`, written into this slice's integration.json.
wiring.handlerEntry: `HudActions.Value(CommandContext, string? session)` is the entry the integration batch calls with the addressed session; the kernel-dispatched `HandleValue(CommandContext)` passes none, which `audience=team` does not need and `audience=self` refuses.

unverified: Whether the shield bar's prefab is wired at all in this build. The interop xref reports `PUI_LocalPlayerStatus.UpdateShield` with a caller count of 2 and the layer's own `PlayerGuiLayer.UpdateShield` wrapper with 0, while the sibling `UpdateHealth`/`UpdateInfection`/`UpdateAir` wrappers each report 1. That is a weak signal (an xref scan is not a call graph) and it points at 'the readout exists but nothing drives it natively', which is exactly the case this row is for — but it has to be seen in game.

The value-to-length mapping of the shield bar: `UpdateShield` takes an absolute value and the bar normalises against `m_shieldValueRef`, whose value is not readable from metadata. `form=bar` may therefore fill the bar wrongly until the game is observed.
Whether `m_shieldUIParent` is on or off by default and whether the status readout's own update resets the bar's position or colour on the next frame.

The geometry of the overhead line: the name mesh's `textBounds` is local to that mesh and the -4 offset under it is `ResourceHudView`'s own number. Four players on screen at once, edge clamping, and a downed or grabbed teammate all move the name mesh in ways only the game shows.

The refresh cadence of `UpdateExtraInfo`: it is the game's own refresh point, and it is not known how often it runs per second or whether a value written while the marker is hidden is redrawn when it comes back.

The local-session comparison: `SNet.LocalPlayer.Lookup` is the same spelling the network layer addresses a presentation request with, but a machine with no local player (`HasLocalPlayer` false) and a bot's own key are both refused rather than presented, and whether a bot can ever be the addressee of a `self` step is a question for the integration batch.

Hidden states (Tab, a terminal, the pause menu, being downed) and resolution changes: `FocusStateManager` and `UI_IOnResolutionChange` are the game's own mechanisms for both, and this row registers with neither; the overhead line follows the name mesh's own `activeInHierarchy` instead.

What happens when `InfiniTweaks`' own resource line is enabled at the same time: both clone a native TMP and both postfix `UpdateExtraInfo`, and neither knows about the other. `ResourceHud` clears `m_extraInfo` and rewrites the name; this row writes neither, so the two may still fight over the extra-information row's visibility.
repoPrecedent: InfiniTweaks\ResourceHud.cs + ResourceHudView.cs: a postfix on PlaceNavMarkerOnGO.UpdateExtraInfo, a clone of NavMarker.m_playerName, saved-and-restored native visibility — the teammate-overhead path this row now implements.
ForgeRuntime\Framework\RuntimeKernel.Presentation.cs: the tier this row is declared on, with its 64-recipient and 512-byte limits and its rule that a presentation write commits nothing.
ForgeRuntime\GameBindings\NetworkCommandRouting.cs: the endpoint slot a presentation request is addressed by, and the local-session comparison `audience=self` repeats at the handler.
